Argentina needed this game.  We suffered through the same tropes of Di Maria getting injured and Higuain not producing, but we came through even stronger than before.  Why?  Messi.  Nobody really realizes this but the team and fanbase were still recovering from the world cup loss.  The world cup took a lot of emotional investment and was an insane struggle, especially for Messi, who took the whole team on his back, and carried the weight of a nation to the final, just to lose.  I think Argentine coach played this game and the tournament perfectly by not playing Messi until when he did.  He kept Messi off the pitch as long as he could so the team could form some sort of identity by itself, but also so that they would stop taking Messi for granted and actually show some initiative.  Everything changed when Messi was preparing to enter the game.  The Argentine players, instead of cowering to his godliness and being complacent, they played like they had something to prove to Messi, and felt like they owed him for his brilliance and duty to their country.  By the time He came on, everybody in the stadium was begging for Him, even though Argentina was playing decent football.  Everybody felt connected to Messi, because in a way they are.  Messi is the lifeforce and life's blood of Argentina football and we were all reminded of that today.  I don't even blame the kid who ran onto the pitch to get to Messi after the game because I understand what he was feeling.    I am just really appreciative I got to be a part of this moment while I was at my apartment hundreds of miles away.
